set.hook: Éric Canino's two-star terrace at La Réserve Ramatuelle: Guérard-school cooking, olive oil not butter.
set.why: Canino learned from Michel Guérard, who turned lightness into a haute-cuisine idea at Eugénie-les-Bains, and he has run this kitchen at Michel Reybier's La Réserve for more than fifteen years. The second star came in January 2020 and still holds. The 2026 season ran from 1 May to 11 October, every day, so the room on the Quessine hill is dark now; the vegetable menu goes from first bite to dessert without meat or fish.

set.hook: The one-star table of a Gigaro wine estate, set menus cooked from its own organic kitchen garden.
set.why: The Rocchietta-Montloin family has owned Château de Valmer since 1946, and the estate still makes its own Côtes de Provence. La Palmeraie seats about forty under the old palm grove or on a terrace over the gardens, and every menu starts from the organic potager a few steps away. set.hook: Two ex-Vague d'Or cooks in a village room above the pool; despite the name, open all year.
set.why: Florent Manini spent about seven years as pastry chef to Arnaud Donckele at La Vague d'Or, and both he and Anna Thillaye did winters at Sébastien Vauxion's Sarkara in Courchevel. Lunch moves to the pool bar from May to September, and two theme nights a week, a barbecue and a Mediterranean sharing table, change the room's pace.

summit.title: Stars above the bay
summit.story: The decorated tables around Cavalaire all sit inside hotels, and all three keep summer hours. La Voile, at La Réserve Ramatuelle, has held two stars since 2020 for Éric Canino, a Michel Guérard pupil, and in 2026 opened from 1 May to 11 October. La Palmeraie, on the Château de Valmer wine estate above Gigaro, keeps one star in 2026 and cooks from its own organic garden; it served from 8 May to 4 October, and the estate has brought in Thomas Pezeril to sign its menus. Vista, at Lily of the Valley on the same hillside, has no star but a Gault&Millau 13/20 in 2026, and Sisteron lamb to share.
summit.where: La Voile, Ramatuelle; La Palmeraie, La Croix-Valmer; Vista, La Croix-Valmer

chefs.title: Two chefs' rooms
chefs.story: Away from the beaches, two smaller rooms carry their cooks' names more than a view. Les Saisonniers, in La Croix-Valmer village above the municipal pool, opened in early 2024 when Florent Manini, long Arnaud Donckele's pastry chef at La Vague d'Or, and Anna Thillaye went out on their own; despite its name it opens all year, Wednesday to Saturday, and is in the MICHELIN selection. In Cavalaire itself, Le Parc at the renovated Hôtel du Parc is an evening table under the pines where Jean-Brice Ruffroy cooks a southern bistronomic carte; it ran from 24 April to 3 October 2026 and is closed now.
chefs.where: Les Saisonniers, La Croix-Valmer; Le Parc, Cavalaire-sur-Mer

sand.title: Lunch on the sand
sand.story: The bay's beach tables run from spring to autumn and cook what suits a terrace: grilled fish, salads, a pasta. La Pinède Plage, the beach restaurant of a hotel at Gigaro, holds one Gault&Millau toque (12/20, 2025) for an octopus carpaccio, and its 2026 season ran from 30 April to 10 October. At the far end of the same beach, Marius à la plage has been run by Arthur and Sarah since 2012 and grills squid and sardines with house ratatouille; it shut on 30 September. On Cavalaire's Grande Plage, Tamaris Beach serves plancha fish under a straw roof and has the longest season of the three, into late October or early November.
sand.where: La Pinède Plage, La Croix-Valmer; Marius à la plage, La Croix-Valmer; Tamaris Beach, Cavalaire-sur-Mer
